metadata.title: React Context Setup for Game State

story.iWant: I want React Context providers for game state and progression state
story.soThat: so that components can access and update game state throughout the application

tasks.task: Create GameContext - Create `src/contexts/` directory if it doesn't exist - Create `src/contexts/GameContext.tsx` file - Import `GameState` type from `src/types/game.ts` - Define `GameContext` using `createContext<GameStateContextValue | null>(null)` - Define `GameStateContextValue` interface with game state and update functions - Create `GameProvider` component that wraps children - Use `useState` or `useReducer` for game state management - Implement update functions: setCoziness, setTimeRemaining, setScore, addEvent, removeEvent - Set initial state matching default game state (coziness: 60, timeRemaining: 60-90, score: 0, activeEvents: [], isPlaying: false, isPaused: false, gameOver: false) - Export `GameContext`, `GameProvider`, and custom hook `useGame()`

Create ProgressionContext - Create `src/contexts/ProgressionContext.tsx` file - Import `ProgressionState` type from `src/types/progression.ts` - Define `ProgressionContext` using `createContext<ProgressionStateContextValue | null>(null)` - Define `ProgressionStateContextValue` interface with progression state and update functions - Create `ProgressionProvider` component that wraps children - Use `useState` or `useReducer` for progression state management - Implement update functions: addXP, levelUp, addSvitlyachky, purchaseItem, unlockAchievement - Set initial state to load from localStorage or use defaults (level: 1, xp: 0, svitlyachky: 0, purchasedItems: [], equippedItems: {}, achievements: []) - Note: localStorage integration will be added in Story 1.4, for now use defaults or placeholder - Export `ProgressionContext`, `ProgressionProvider`, and custom hook `useProgression()`

Verify hook usage for state management - Verify GameContext uses `useState` or `useReducer` hook - Verify ProgressionContext uses `useState` or `useReducer` hook - Ensure no direct state mutations (use functional updates) - Consider useReducer for complex state updates (game events, progression updates)

Test provider composition - Create test example or verify providers can be nested - Test: <ProgressionProvider><GameProvider>...</GameProvider></ProgressionProvider> - Test: <GameProvider><ProgressionProvider>...</ProgressionProvider></GameProvider> - Verify both contexts can be consumed independently - Verify contexts work when composed together

Export TypeScript types - Export `GameStateContextValue` interface/type from GameContext.tsx - Export `ProgressionStateContextValue` interface/type from ProgressionContext.tsx - Export custom hooks `useGame()` and `useProgression()` with proper return types - Ensure TypeScript types enable autocomplete and type checking in IDEs - Add JSDoc comments for context value interfaces

Testing & Validation - Verify TypeScript compilation succeeds: `npm run build` or `npx tsc --noEmit` - Ensure no TypeScript errors or warnings in context files - Test contexts can be imported and used in other components - Verify initial state values are correct - Test update functions work correctly (manually or with temporary test component) - Check that contexts are ready for use in Story 2.1 (Game Loop)

doc.title: Story 1.3: React Context Setup for Game State

docs.doc: Story specification with acceptance criteria, tasks, and dev notes. Includes detailed implementation guidance for creating GameContext and ProgressionContext providers.

Architecture decision to use React Context API instead of Redux. Guidance on using useState or useReducer for state management. Context re-renders all consumers - manage with care to prevent performance issues.

Exact GameState and ProgressionState structure definitions. Initial state values: GameState (coziness: 60, timeRemaining: 60-90, score: 0, activeEvents: [], isPlaying: false, isPaused: false, gameOver: false), ProgressionState (level: 1, xp: 0, svitlyachky: 0, purchasedItems: [], equippedItems: {}, achievements: []).
Architecture decision record explaining rationale for React Context over Redux. Simple state management needs, no extra dependencies, sufficient for hackathon scope.
Project structure showing contexts directory location: `src/contexts/GameContext.tsx` and `src/contexts/ProgressionContext.tsx`. File naming conventions: PascalCase for component files.
PRD requirement: Local component state + simple context or hooks. No Redux needed for MVP. Keep state management simple and straightforward.
Epic-level story definition with acceptance criteria and technical notes. Prerequisites: Story 1.2. Context should be ready for use in Story 2.1.

Previous story learnings: Type definitions complete and ready. GameState, ProgressionState, and GameEvent types are defined and exported. TypeScript strict mode enabled. Import pattern: Use `import type` for type-only imports.

artifact.reason: GameState interface defines the structure for game context state. Includes coziness, timeRemaining, score, activeEvents, isPlaying, isPaused, gameOver properties.
ProgressionState interface defines the structure for progression context state. Includes level, xp, svitlyachky, purchasedItems, equippedItems, achievements properties.
EquippedItems interface defines the structure for equipped cosmetic items. Used within ProgressionState.equippedItems property.
GameEvent interface defines the structure for events in activeEvents array. Required for GameState.activeEvents property type.
EventType union type defines valid event types. Used in GameEvent.type property.
EventPriority union type defines valid priority levels. Used in GameEvent.priority property.
Contexts directory location. Currently empty - needs to be created. Will contain GameContext.tsx and ProgressionContext.tsx files.

constraints.constraint: State Management Approach: Use React Context API for global state (no Redux per PRD). Follow architecture document "State Management" section. Use `useState` for simple state or `useReducer` for complex state updates. Context re-renders all consumers - manage with care to prevent performance issues.

Context Structure: GameContext manages coziness, timeRemaining, score, activeEvents, isPlaying, isPaused, gameOver. ProgressionContext manages level, xp, svitlyachky, purchasedItems, equippedItems, achievements. Both contexts provide typed update functions for state modifications.

Context Provider Pattern: Create Context with `createContext<T | null>(null)` (null initial value). Provider component wraps children and provides context value. Custom hook (e.g., `useGame()`) wraps `useContext()` and handles null check. Export Context, Provider, and custom hook for clean API.

Update Functions: Use functional updates: `setState(prev => newValue)` to avoid stale closures. For complex updates (event management, progression calculations), consider `useReducer`. Update functions should be stable (use `useCallback` if needed, or rely on React's memoization). Functions should handle edge cases (e.g., removeEvent should handle non-existent events gracefully).

Type Safety: Context value types must match GameState and ProgressionState interfaces exactly. Custom hooks return typed context value (not null after provider check). Export context value types for use in components. Follow TypeScript best practices from Story 1.2.

Initial State: GameContext uses default game state (game not started). ProgressionContext loads from localStorage or uses defaults (localStorage integration in Story 1.4). For Story 1.3: Use default values, note that localStorage integration comes in Story 1.4.

Provider Composition: Providers can be nested in any order (both compositions should work). Components can consume both contexts independently. Prepare for App.tsx to wrap application with both providers.

File Naming: PascalCase for context files (matches component naming convention). Directory structure matches architecture document. Context files: `src/contexts/GameContext.tsx`, `src/contexts/ProgressionContext.tsx`.
TypeScript Strict Mode: TypeScript strict mode is enabled - all types must be properly defined. Use `import type` for type-only imports. No `any` types allowed.

interface.name: GameStateContextValue
interface.signature: interface GameStateContextValue { gameState: GameState; setCoziness: (value: number) => void; setTimeRemaining: (value: number) => void; setScore: (value: number) => void; addEvent: (event: GameEvent) => void; removeEvent: (eventId: string) => void; ... }

interface.name: ProgressionStateContextValue
interface.signature: interface ProgressionStateContextValue { progressionState: ProgressionState; addXP: (amount: number) => void; levelUp: () => void; addSvitlyachky: (amount: number) => void; purchaseItem: (itemId: string) => void; unlockAchievement: (achievementId: string) => void; ... }

tests.standards: TypeScript compilation must succeed with no errors. Use `npm run build` or `npx tsc --noEmit` to verify. No TypeScript errors or warnings in context files. Test contexts can be imported and used in other components. Verify initial state values are correct. Test update functions work correctly (manually or with temporary test component). Contexts should be ready for use in Story 2.1 (Game Loop). Consider using Vitest for unit tests (from architecture document), but manual testing is acceptable for this foundational story.
tests.locations: Test files should be co-located with source files: `src/contexts/GameContext.test.tsx` and `src/contexts/ProgressionContext.test.tsx` (optional for this story). Manual testing via temporary test components is acceptable.
